title: Making Reality Fracture Draft Look Easy!!!
event: FRA live Arena draft, solo; the Arena pick timer is on and chat is not mentioned; Premier / Quick not named on screen
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/kMo5X6G9lAU (banner strips and pack title rows; layout pool-at-right to P1p5, then pack on top with the pool below; the 40/40 deck screen at 1251 s; the sideboard is not shown); takes from the transcript, the pool counts and the deck screen; hover popups hid some cards; transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; cut-off 1255 s (the 40/40 deck screen is on at 1230 and 1251)

colour_path.quote: I do really like blue decks in this format.
blue is looking decently open ... white's looking maybe open.
pick five is a signal that black might be open.
I would rather splash green than red.
the better my deck gets, the less likely it is that I will want to splash.
Nobody else is playing blue black.

picks.reasoning: Plan for All Outcomes over Dark Matter Manipulator: really strong as a kill spell that later lets you surveil on every noncreature spell; blue works with red, white and black Jace decks. His order from the pack: Plan, the rare, Hexhaven Battalion, Way of the Mind Sculptor; Unsummon and Hexhaven Battalion are the commons he likes; Greenhouse Propagator is far behind.

considered.Dark Matter Manipulator: a one-mana 3/2 a lot of the time; not as good as Plan
considered.Hexhaven Battalion: decent gap, the common he likes
considered.Unsummon: decent gap, the second Unsummon is much less valuable

quotes: I think I go plan for all outcomes, then maybe the rare, then Hexhaven battalion, then way of the mind sculptor.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment over Stingcaster Mage: easy to build a good Recruitment deck with Plan for All Outcomes, splashable in blue-green, one of the best win conditions at common or uncommon for a graveyard strategy; Stingcaster is a 2/1 that draws a card while Recruitment makes two 2/2s and flashes back. They can combo (flash Recruitment back with Stingcaster).

considered.Stingcaster Mage: loves it but only a 2/1 that draws a card
considered.Mabel, Bitter Recluse: fine, usually they have used their Jace

quotes: I like recursive recruitment here. The uncommon multicolored card over sting caster mage.

picks.reasoning: Mindseeker Oculus: he has a rule to almost never pass Oculus; even if he were not blue-black it works with the Plan; Proft would be second and Your Fate Ends Here is also good; blue looks open and white maybe open; no information from pairings since the pair is still in the pack.

considered.Proft, Consulting Detective: he would take it second from this pack

quotes: I have a rule for myself and that's like almost never pass Mindseeker Oculus.

picks.reasoning: Rewrite Regrets: a card he has gone on a roller coaster with; the landcyclers are very playable and the black one is especially good to get back with it (cycle on turn two, get back a 6/4 menace on turn four); he would not mind Twinned Vision; Way of the Necromancer feels almost unplayable but he likes it; keeping taking good blue and black cards.

considered.Twinned Vision: really good in the midrange deck, not a card he wants more than one of

quotes: The cyclingers are very playable in this format ... you cycle it on turn two, turn four, you get back a 6/4 menace.

picks.reasoning: Extended Absence: really good removal and a sign black may be open: it is the best black common and still in the pack at pick five with plenty of uncommons left; other cards in his space are green (Marwyn, Restore with Empathy, Bestial Incursion).

considered.Marwyn, the Preserver: green card he could maybe splash

quotes: Extended absence. Really, really good removal spell. ... pick five is a signal that black might be open.

picks.reasoning: Apex Witchstalker over Icy Reception: a really good combo with Rewrite Regrets and a card he does not mind casting at the top of the curve to reach the Recruitments; Icy Reception is a card he has gone on a journey with and now rates middle; Hexhaven Battalion not preferred.

considered.Hexhaven Battalion: no reason to take over the two

quotes: I'm going to take the Apex Witchstalker though. I think this card's really a good combo with Rewrite Regrets.

picks.reasoning: Apex Witchstalker (second) over Wrath of the Bloodmane: in this deck with graveyard synergy he would rather splash green than red, and he has a couple of landcyclers to get it done.
quotes: I would rather splash green than red. And so I'll just take this card.

picks.reasoning: Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows ('Euro') over Sphinx's Approach: extra board presence, fills the graveyard; he might not play it; he does not think he is likely to play Sphinx's Approach either.

considered.Sphinx's Approach: not his favourite, lots of do-nothings already

quotes: I'm going to take Eureko over the Sphinx's Approach. Just give myself some extra board presence.

picks.reasoning: Dark Matter Manipulator wheeled: 'that's a pickup'; it fuels his graveyard and gives him a one-drop; he could splash white again, but green is his hope for Hapatra.
quotes: Wow, we wield dark matter manipulator. That's a pickup for sure.

picks.reasoning: Afterthought Sentry (a two-drop he needs, opponents have flashback cards); he does not expect to play it ('straight in the sideboard'); he says he takes it so as not to send a black signal.

considered.Kiora of Salt and Sand: not a card he would want to splash

quotes: I don't have any two drops. This one can get the job done.

picks.reasoning: Taken card not identified: he says he takes 'the black card' so as not to send a black signal; none of Rampart Hunter, Tether Technician or Wrecking Gecko is in the final pool, so the take was probably the Swamp.
quotes: I guess I'll take the black card just so I don't send a black signal.

picks.reasoning: Stingerquill Annex (black-red land): a land is a good pick whoever passed this pack; with three cards left he would not normally expect to see it.
quotes: Black red land is nice though. This is always just like a thing in draft.

picks.reasoning: Vigorbloom Annex over Restore with Empathy: you never know what happens; he does not want to splash Restore.
quotes: Here I'll take Vigorbloom Annex. You never know what's going to happen.

picks.reasoning: Last card auto-selected; never displayed.

Seasoned Cryomancer (mythic) over Theorix Charm: he would take the charm if there were no mythic that fits his strategy; Cryomancer works with Apex Witchstalker (discard to reanimate later); he thinks a Charm may wheel since nobody else seems to be blue-black.

considered.Theorix Charm: loves it, would take it if the mythic were absent; expects to wheel one
considered.Rescue Girl, First Responder: likely to be taken by someone

quotes: I would definitely take the charm if there wasn't a mythic rare that really fits my strategy well.

picks.reasoning: Countersculpt over Gallia, Tragic Host: perfect for his control deck even with few Jace cards; Gallia second, a two-drop that can come back; Unsummon he would play but only ever wants one.
quotes: Counter sculpt is a great card though. I also like Gallia, but I think counter sculpt is perfect for my control deck.

picks.reasoning: Countersculpt again over Last Gasp, Dark Matter Manipulator and Gallia: keeps taking Counter Sculpts, a really strong card for a deck trying to go long; three black cards in the pack so one may wheel (it does: Dark Matter Manipulator).
quotes: I think I'm just going to keep taking counter sculpts. It's a really strong card.

picks.reasoning: Last Gasp: he just needs the kill spell and instant speed makes it better than Proft for his deck; Proft is good but he would not use him as effectively.

considered.Proft, Consulting Detective: good, but he needs the kill spell

quotes: Yeah, I just need the kill spell, especially instant speed makes it...

picks.reasoning: Stingerquill Charm over Semester Foreseer: a two-mana deal three; maybe he splashes black (sic: red), maybe not; he does not need a random four-drop.

considered.Semester Foreseer: does not think it is very good

quotes: Here, I will take stinger quill charm maybe over semester foreseer.

picks.reasoning: Proft, Sinister Mastermind over Surveillance Phantasm: easy pick, minus three minus one kills many creatures; he can move it to the one-drop slot.
quotes: Easy pick here. It's just like the one mana mode's pretty good.

picks.reasoning: Theoretical Necromancer: he likes one copy of the necromancer in these decks when milling himself; Eureko maybe okay; does not like Massacre Girl much.

considered.Massacre Girl, Most Wanted: does not like it that much

quotes: I do like one copy of the necromancer in these decks if I'm milling myself.

picks.reasoning: Theorix Charm eighth pick (the second Charm wheel is hoped for); he could have taken a two/three flyer, but it is better if you are surveilling actively.
quotes: Ooh, so we got a theorix charm eighth pick. Can we get one ninth pick?

picks.reasoning: Theorix Charm wheeled: 'Did I wheel it? Bang.' The other card he thought might wheel was the land; the deck is getting special.

considered.Formidable Commons: the land he thought might wheel

quotes: Did I wheel it? Did I wheel it? Bang.

picks.reasoning: Gallia, Tragic Host over Unsummon: Gallia fits the mill plan and the theme, he needs two-drops; he only ever wants one Unsummon in this kind of deck.

considered.Unsummon: would be a good card but only one wanted

quotes: I think I'm going to take Gallia over Unsummon here.

picks.reasoning: Dark Matter Manipulator wheeled again: 'when you think you can wheel cards, you get so much value'; he wanted the Charm, thought it could wheel and got Cryomancer instead.
quotes: Bang. We wield the dark matter manipulator.

picks.reasoning: Infinite Coursework: a marginal card but unconditional removal for many things; he thinks it makes the cut; 18 playables now.
quotes: Infinite coursework is honestly a card that's more marginal, but I still think it's going to make the cut.

considered.Silence the Echo: five-mana kill spell, might be better than coursework
